tools.name: get_codex_domain
tools.description: Return the full markdown overview of one Codex cybersecurity domain identified by slug. The Codex is Techimpossible's prerequisite graph of security capabilities — compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, ISO 42001) are views into it. Pair with list_codex_domains to discover valid slugs.

tools.name: recommend_framework
tools.description:
Opinionated framework recommendation from Techimpossible.

Asks the qualifying questions a real cybersecurity consultant asks on a scope call: 6 high-level routing questions (sector, AI involvement, customer profile, customer geographies, regulated data in scope, deal driver, org stage) plus 24 Codex foundational controls (6 per inventory: people, vendors, AI, data).

Returns a Codex-grounded recommendation: per-inventory foundational readiness, per-control state with what each missing control blocks, a primary program (which may legitimately be 'build foundation first' via Cybersecurity Fundamentals), queued recommendations with sequencing rationale, and an honest 'what we did not recommend' section.

Start here if you don't know which framework you need or want Techimpossible's perspective. Call gap_assess directly if you already know your framework.

sector.description: Primary industry the company operates in.

ai_involvement.description: How AI is used in the company. Explicit, never inferred. 'none' = no AI; 'internal_only' = Copilot/Cursor/Claude in workflows but not in product; 'customer_facing' = AI feature in product; 'core_product' = AI is the product.

customer_geographies.description: Where the company's customers are based. Multi-select.

data_in_scope.description: Regulated or sensitive data classes the company handles. Multi-select. Use ['none'] if none apply.

deadline.description: Free-text deadline if any, e.g. 'Q3 enterprise renewal'.

current_state_notes.description: Optional free-text colour about the current state — existing certifications, prior audit history, anything the structured fields didn't capture.

foundational_checks.description: Answers to the 24 Codex foundational controls (6 per inventory: people, vendors, ai, data). Ask the prospect each question; record "present" / "partial" / "absent" / "unknown" honestly. "unknown" is a valid signal that surfaces as a thing to resolve.

current_org_chart.description: Do you maintain a current org chart that reflects every employee, contractor, and their reporting line?

idp_hr_reconciliation.description: Is your IdP / SSO directory reconciled against your HR system of record on a regular cadence (weekly or better)?

jml_process.description: Do you have a documented joiner / mover / leaver workflow with named owners and SLAs?

contractor_inventory.description: Do you maintain a current list of contractors, the systems they access, and contract end dates?

production_admin_inventory.description: Can you produce, on demand, a list of every person with administrative access to production systems?

quarterly_access_review.description: Do quarterly access reviews actually happen, with documented sign-off from system owners?

vendor_list_complete.description: Do you maintain a current list of every third-party SaaS, processor, sub-processor, and infrastructure provider in use?

vendor_tiering.description: Are vendors tiered by data sensitivity and integration depth (e.g. tier-1 critical, tier-2 important, tier-3 incidental)?

subprocessor_disclosure.description: Do you maintain a subprocessor list and disclose it to enterprise customers when required by contract?

tier_1_security_evidence.description: Do you have current SOC 2 Type II reports (or equivalent ISO 27001 certificates) on file for your tier-1 vendors?

vendor_review_cadence.description: Do you re-review your tier-1 vendors at least annually, and after any public incident (breach, regulator action, ownership change)?

dpa_inventory.description: Are your Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) and Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) catalogued by vendor, current, and accessible?

ai_tool_inventory.description: Can you produce a list of every AI tool actually used by employees (Copilot, Cursor, Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, paid SaaS with AI features, etc.)?

ai_use_policy.description: Do you have a written policy on what data can and cannot be sent to consumer AI tools, with role-based access to sanctioned alternatives?

ai_features_in_saas_audit.description: Have you audited your existing SaaS subscriptions for AI features added in the last 12 months (most have shipped some)?

ai_in_product_register.description: Do you maintain a register of every AI system used in your product, including model provider, data inputs, and decision impact level?

ai_human_oversight.description: For high-impact AI decisions, is there a documented human-in-the-loop or human-on-the-loop requirement?

ai_vendor_questions.description: Have you updated your vendor questionnaire to ask vendors about AI in their pipelines (their data your AI sees; their AI your data flows through)?

data_classification_scheme.description: Do you have a documented data classification scheme (e.g. Public / Internal / Confidential / Restricted), with classification applied to actual data?

data_flow_diagrams.description: Do you maintain data flow diagrams that show how customer data moves through your systems, including third parties?

regulated_data_inventory.description: Do you maintain an explicit map of where regulated data (PHI, EU/UK PII, financial, IP/trade-secret) is stored and processed?

ropa_for_gdpr.description: If you process EU or UK personal data, do you maintain Records of Processing Activities (Article 30 RoPA)?

data_retention_policies.description: Are data retention policies defined per data class and technically enforced (not just documented)?

dpia_process.description: Do you have a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) process for new uses of personal data, with named approvers?

tools.name: gap_assess
tools.description:
Express-path gap assessment against a known target framework.

Pass the framework (soc2, iso27001, hipaa, iso42001), AI involvement (explicit), and answers to the 24 Codex foundational controls. Returns a Codex-grounded report: a 2-3 sentence framing of what the framework covers, foundational readiness per inventory and per control (with what each missing control blocks), the recommended starting point (which may be Cybersecurity Fundamentals first if foundational inventories are incomplete), an ISO 42001 stacking recommendation when AI is in product, and a scope-call brief.

Operational/advanced/expert tier gaps are intentionally not assessed by this tool — they require deep framework knowledge and live-stack inspection that belong on the scope call. The foundational tier is the substance.

If you don't yet know your framework — or want Techimpossible's perspective on which fits — call recommend_framework first.

tools.name: get_codex_dependencies
tools.description: Page through canonical prerequisite edges. from must precede to; hard is required, soft is recommended. Omit slug for all edges. tools.name: get_codex_pareto

tools.description: Page through explicitly public catalogue control IDs, Techimpossible briefs, scope mapping hints and evidence expectations. No invented equivalence mappings.
